title: Data Diode Transfers
description: Moves data across the gap with hardware data diodes that physically allow one direction only. Fiber with the return path removed cannot be subverted by software; it is the strongest one-way guarantee. High-security networks standardize on them.

demo.title: Demo — Data Diode Transfers

title: One-Way Protocols
description: Runs protocols designed for one-way flow: UDP streams, file drops, no acknowledgments. The sender never expects a reply; reliability comes from redundancy. It matches the diode's physics.

demo.title: Demo — One-Way Protocols

title: QR Code Bridges
description: Bridges small payloads with QR codes scanned across the gap. Keys and signatures fit in a few codes; cameras never touch the secure network. It is the human-speed air gap.

demo.title: Demo — QR Code Bridges

title: Sneakernet Protocols
description: Moves data on physical media with chain-of-custody protocols. Encrypted drives travel by courier; every handoff is logged and verified. Bandwidth is a truck; latency is a day.

demo.title: Demo — Sneakernet Protocols

title: Optical Transfer
description: Transfers data optically — screen to camera — with no electrical connection. Light crosses the gap; malware cannot ride photons back. It is slow and very sure.

demo.title: Demo — Optical Transfer

title: Manual Key Ceremonies
description: Generates and transfers keys in witnessed ceremonies with split knowledge. No single person ever holds the whole key; the ceremony is scripted and recorded. Root keys are born this way.

demo.title: Demo — Manual Key Ceremonies

title: Cross-Domain Guards
description: Filters transfers through cross-domain guards that inspect content deeply. Guards validate formats, strip active content, and enforce policies per direction. They are the firewall of the air gap.

demo.title: Demo — Cross-Domain Guards

title: File Sanitization (CDR)
description: Rebuilds files with content disarm and reconstruction to strip embedded threats. CDR discards the original and builds a clean copy; macros and exploits do not survive. Every file crossing gets rebuilt.

demo.title: Demo — File Sanitization (CDR)

title: USB Data Blockers
description: Blocks USB data pins with charge-only adapters to stop malware and exfiltration. Power flows; data does not. It is the simplest port protection.

demo.title: Demo — USB Data Blockers

title: TEMPEST Considerations
description: Accounts for electromagnetic emanations that can bridge air gaps. Shielding, zoning, and emission limits keep signals inside; red/black separation is the discipline. Air gaps leak through physics.

demo.title: Demo — TEMPEST Considerations

title: Transfer Auditing
description: Audits every gap crossing with what, when, who, and authorization. The audit trail proves the gap's integrity; gaps without auditing are just slow networks. Every crossing is an event.

demo.title: Demo — Transfer Auditing

title: Scheduled Sync Windows
description: Opens the gap only during scheduled, supervised sync windows. Outside the window the gap is complete; during it, transfers run under watch. It bounds exposure in time.

demo.title: Demo — Scheduled Sync Windows

title: Hardware-Enforced Directionality
description: Enforces transfer direction in hardware that software cannot override. Optical isolators and one-way taps make the direction a physical fact. Policy becomes physics.

demo.title: Demo — Hardware-Enforced Directionality

title: Air-Gap Incident Response
description: Responds to suspected gap breaches with containment that assumes the worst. The bridge is severed first; forensics follows. Air-gap incidents are rare and serious.

demo.title: Demo — Air-Gap Incident Response

title: Acoustic Mesh Caution
description: Treats acoustic and other covert channels as in-scope threats to air gaps. Researchers have exfiltrated via speakers, fans, and LEDs; defenses monitor for anomalous emanations. Paranoia is calibrated to the asset.

demo.title: Demo — Acoustic Mesh Caution
